headline: Only 72.4 % are employed, well below both benchmarks, and 17.2 % are still seeking work.
how_to_read: Flows run from all respondents (left) to employed or not employed (middle) and then to detailed situation (right); width is the share of respondents. The hatched "Hidden" flow marks situations held back because fewer than 3 people fall into them.
key_findings: Full-time work accounts for 58.6 % of respondents, within the 72.4 % employed.
Seeking work, at 17.2 %, makes up most of the 27.6 % not employed; no respondents are students or retired.
benchmark: Employment trails the Asia figure (91.3 %) by 18.9 pp and all schools (92.6 %) by 20.2 pp. The seeking-work share sits 10.6 pp above Asia (6.6 %).
caveats: With n = 29, each person moves the percentages by several points; part-time, self-employed, other employment and not seeking work are hidden (fewer than 3 people).
